Physics: The section is well spread across mechanics, electrostatics/current electricity, magnetism, optics, thermal physics and modern physics, and every key I could verify independently (Q1–Q8, Q10–Q29) is arithmetically and conceptually correct, including the multi-step Wheatstone-bridge, two-liquid buoyancy and stepped-wire items. Difficulty sits at the right BITSAT level: most items are single-concept 30–60 s calculations, with a handful of genuine two-step problems (Q13, Q14, Q23, Q29) providing discrimination without exceeding the ~90 s budget. Only fixes needed are the duplicated 36%-gravity scenario (Q21/Q28) and the LaTeX escaping in Q30; the figure-dependent items (Q9, Q19, Q20, Q24) should be given a final visual check against their artwork before printing.

[minor] This item reuses the identical "g decreases by 36%" scenario of Q21 (and the same 0.25/25% numerical answer), so the pair effectively repeats one percentage-in-g computation; change the percentage or the quantity asked in one of them.
[minor] The LaTeX contains doubled backslashes ($\\mu$, $10\\ \\text{cm}$ in the stem and options) that will print as literal backslashes instead of rendering.

Chemistry: Coverage across physical, inorganic and organic chemistry is broad and every key that can be checked from the text is correct, with numericals (q42, q43, q51, q59) pitched at a sensible BITSAT level. The section is, however, over-weighted on d-block/coordination recall (q33, q40, q44, q54, q55) and contains two essentially identical unpaired-electron counts, plus one overlong statement item and one out-of-syllabus test. Also note the answer-key skew — 13 of 30 keys are option C — which should be redistributed before printing.

[minor] Four multi-clause statements (hybridisation + shape + two hydrolysis routes + redox bookkeeping) make this too dense for a ~90 s item; cut to three statements, ideally dropping I, whose XeF2/XeF4 VSEPR shapes are already probed in q31.

[minor] The options read "A < B", comparing the metals rather than the quantities asked about, so they should be written as φ_A < φ_B (with the two lines labelled A and B in the figure); the photoelectric stopping-potential framing also sits oddly in a Chemistry section.

[minor] Barfoed's test (copper acetate/acetic acid, 2-minute timing) is outside the NCERT/BITSAT biomolecules scope and rewards obscure recall rather than the reducing-sugar chemistry the syllabus expects.

[minor] This duplicates q40, since both items reduce to counting unpaired electrons in a d^n ion; replace it with a distinct coordination-compounds concept (isomerism, EAN, or spectrochemical-series ordering).

English Proficiency: The section covers the expected BITSAT spread (two vocabulary completions, synonym, antonym, idiom, two grammar-error items, a para jumble and a two-question comprehension set), and every intended key is defensible with no duplicate testing points. Difficulty is skewed easy, however: items 64, 68 and 70 have three transparently wrong distractors each, so a strong candidate can clear them in seconds. Tightening the distractors in the synonym/antonym and completion items (e.g. nearer-synonym foils) would bring the section closer to the actual paper's discrimination level.
[minor] The stem's phrase "a coherent paragraph formed by them" has an unclear antecedent; reword to "...the opening sentence of the coherent paragraph formed by these four sentences?"

[minor] The stem asks what can be "inferred", but the key is a near-verbatim restatement of "A wetland that has been filled or cut off from its natural water flows may provide little protection", so either change the stem to "According to the passage..." or make the key a genuine inference.

Logical Reasoning: The section has a sensible spread of verbal and non-verbal reasoning (series, coding, syllogisms, blood relations, dictionary order, spatial items) at an appropriate BITSAT level, and every fully text-based item checks out with a unique, correct key solvable well within 90 seconds. The main defect is production-related: q78 and q83 carry no artwork whatsoever, and the other figure-dependent items (71, 74, 79, 80, 82, 88) must be proof-checked against their diagrams before printing. Once the artwork is inserted, confirm that the two odd-figure-out items and the two number-puzzle-in-figure items test genuinely different rules rather than repeating the same idea.
[major] The item has no problem figure and all four options are blank, so the odd-one-out cannot be presented, solved or verified against the key C.
[major] Like q78, this odd-figure-out item is missing its problem figure and all option images, leaving the key C unverifiable and the item unprintable.

Mathematics: All forty keys check out, and the section covers the syllabus broadly with a sensible spread of coordinate geometry, calculus, algebra and probability at roughly BITSAT length (q95, q101, q113 are the longest but still ~90 s items). The main defects are production-level: the broken negation symbols in q118 and the stray LaTeX in q93 must be fixed before printing, plus the "parabolas" slip in q122. Level is slightly light at the bottom end — q98, q116 and q123 are pure formula plug-ins, and q98/q116 duplicate the same transformation idea, so replacing one of them with a substantive item would improve balance.
[minor] The exponent is mis-typeset as "$a+ar+ar^2+ar^3+\text{...}\\\infty$" with a stray backslash/infinity symbol; it should simply read $a+ar+ar^2+\cdots$ to infinity.
[minor] Option (C) $[2,6]$ contains $x=2$, which the stem explicitly deletes from $D$, so it is not an interval in $D$ at all and should be written as $(2,6]$.
[minor] This is essentially the same one-step "linear transformation of a data set" item as q98 (only the statistic changes), so one of the two should be replaced by a genuine statistics question.
[major] Every negation symbol has lost its backslash and prints as "eg" (e.g. "$eg[p\wedge(q\vee r)]$"), leaving the statement and all four options logically meaningless as printed.
[minor] $y=2x$ is a straight line, not a parabola, so the stem should read "the parabola $y=x^2$ and the line $y=2x$".
